subsystems.name: Collector and beam array
subsystems.role: gathers the star's output and re-emits it as a steerable, concentrated beam.
parts: large thin-film mirrors or Fresnel lenses

subsystems.name: Feedstock supply
subsystems.role: delivers the raw material — dust, regolith or broken-up small bodies — to the construction zone.

subsystems.name: Trap and manipulation stage
subsystems.role: holds individual grains or plasma in place without touching them.

subsystems.name: Deposition head
subsystems.role: fuses feedstock into solid, dense material.
parts: shielding against its own thermal radiation

subsystems.name: Structure being grown
subsystems.role: the product: collectors, radiators, habitat shells and trusses.

subsystems.name: Control and power
subsystems.role: coordination and computation across distances of millions of kilometres.

buildSteps.title: Start with a seed factory
buildSteps.detail: Land a small robotic plant on a low-gravity body. It mines local rock and metal, and uses concentrated sunlight for power and heat. Nothing is launched from Earth at scale.

buildSteps.title: Print the first solar collectors
buildSteps.detail: The seed plant makes thin mirror or photovoltaic film and simple trusses, then uses them to make more of itself. This is the step that decides whether the whole scheme is possible: growth must be exponential, not linear.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a collector swarm
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of free-flying collectors are positioned in orbits around the star, each independently steered. Individually they are gossamer-light because structural loads are near zero in free fall.

buildSteps.title: Build the beam array
buildSteps.detail: Some collectors are fitted with lasing or maser media so their gathered sunlight leaves as a tight, coherent beam rather than spreading light. This is the weakest link: a solar-pumped laser needs enormous collector area per unit of output, and waste heat must be radiated away.

buildSteps.title: Deliver feedstock
buildSteps.detail: Electromagnetic mass drivers on a small moon or asteroid fling crushed material toward the construction volume. Trajectories are matched so payloads arrive slowly and are caught, not smashed.

buildSteps.title: Trap and position material
buildSteps.detail: Overlapping focused beams create faint optical forces on each grain. In practice these forces are tiny, so a real machine would combine them with electrostatic or magnetic fields to actually hold and place a particle.

buildSteps.title: Deposit layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: The beam melts or sinters the held feedstock onto the growing surface. Between passes, the part is cooled in a controlled way so it does not warp, and heat is dumped to radiators larger than the object being built.

buildSteps.title: Grow the swarm
buildSteps.detail: Completed collectors are detached and moved to their working orbit, and the freed factory builds the next batch. Over centuries the swarm can approach a large fraction of the star's light.

buildSteps.title: Variant: star-lifting
buildSteps.detail: To move mass off the star itself, a magnetic scoop or beam-driven driver would peel plasma from the surface and fling it outward, to be collected and used as construction material elsewhere in the system.

prerequisites.why: 3D printing has been demonstrated on the International Space Station, but only at kilogram scale with imported feedstock.
nothing has yet mined, refined and mass-produced structural material off Earth.
the whole idea depends on machines that can copy most of themselves from local material.
solar sails such as JAXA's IKAROS in 2010 proved photon pressure works, but the force is minuscule and unsuitable for gripping and shaping matter.
nobody has modelled or tested the stability of a structure spanning millions of kilometres under a star's gravity and radiation.

pathway.milestone: kilogram-scale printing and assembly in orbit
pathway.unlocks: experience with doing manufacturing without gravity or a ground crew.

pathway.milestone: robotic mining and refining on a small body, feeding an in-space factory
pathway.unlocks: structural material that does not have to be launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a self-growing colony of free-flying solar collectors, square kilometres in total
pathway.unlocks: the first meaningful capture of a star's output, and a test of exponential growth.

pathway.milestone: a partial swarm of collectors, with a small fraction of starlight intercepted
pathway.unlocks: power on a scale no planet-based civilisation can reach.

pathway.milestone: star-lifting to move stellar mass into usable orbit
pathway.unlocks: material and lifetime control over the star itself — physics-permitted, engineering-unproven.
